<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via newTab (literal, a string literal in a comment in actionObject))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/README.md`, `packages/spec/liveness/action.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dfd8e398aacfa74b8f401a9186814fec093cf010` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bf38320cf50ec95bd37c10e0250af8bb2a6d01cc` — the merge of head `080df02a51b2ef5c3d2b91f78672d9f915dde622` into base `dfd8e398aacfa74b8f401a9186814fec093cf010`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bf38320cf50ec95bd37c10e0250af8bb2a6d01cc && git checkout bf38320cf50ec95bd37c10e0250af8bb2a6d01cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dfd8e398aacfa74b8f401a9186814fec093cf010 080df02a51b2ef5c3d2b91f78672d9f915dde622 && git checkout -B drift-repro dfd8e398aacfa74b8f401a9186814fec093cf010 && git merge --no-ff 080df02a51b2ef5c3d2b91f78672d9f915dde622

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dfd8e398aacfa74b8f401a9186814fec093cf010
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dfd8e398aacfa74b8f401a9186814fec093cf010` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `080df02a51b2ef5c3d2b91f78672d9f915dde622`

Local-runs: `check:liveness` (head, plus two controls) · `gen:liveness-counts` · `check:objectui-pin-citations` (head, plus a base-src control) · `check-liveness --producer-gap` · `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors` · `check:doc-authoring` · `check:issue-citations` · `check-changeset-no-major` · `check-empty-changeset` · `check-adr-0087-registration` · `check-changeset-fixed` · comment-stripped `transpileModule` diff (3 files, 2 controls each) · structural walk of both ledgers base→head · lint warn-map derivation over both ledgers · the lint and CLI flow-liveness vitest pins (see ③ for how they were measured)

### ① Derived judgments

Reviewed at head `080df02a51b2ef5c3d2b91f78672d9f915dde622` (PR #20328, card #20296) against base `10ea9eb2ed29269fc98fa8bdee6e265906b2caad`, which is also the merge-base, so the PR diff is exactly `git diff base head`: 8 files, +57/−27. `.objectui-sha` is `f8a9d0fb0596f4521076628e2bbfe27e6ce67d52` at both base and head. Every objectui reading was taken with `git show` / `git grep` against that pin in the read-only clone at `/home/user/objectui` (its HEAD `5c61e524` on an unrelated branch, never switched, unchanged after every gate run), and controlled at objectui `256b4c9ef518dd124760825072c039c687d69113` (the PR's control) and at that clone's `origin/main` `972c1685ec06fa538f29c078f8c3c475089e7856`. The clone is shallow, so pin → main ancestry is not asserted. Gates ran in a detached worktree at the head under the scratchpad (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, exit 0); heavy build and test went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`; the worktree was removed afterwards.

**1. Each flipped row names a real, MOUNTED reader at the pin `f8a9d0fb` — RIGHT.**

Mount chain, closed by hand at the pin, once for both `onSuccess` rows:
- `apps/console/src/main.tsx:155` renders the `I18nProvider` element with `loadLanguage={loadLanguage}` around the `App` element; `apps/console/src/App.tsx:194–421` renders the `ConsoleShell` element around the app content.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/ConsoleShell.tsx:86` calls `useConsoleActionRuntime({ dataSource })` and at `:88–105` mounts the `ActionProvider` element with `onNavigate={runtime.actionProviderProps.onNavigate}` and a `handlers` prop, with `{runtime.dialogs}` inside it.
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:129` is the hook; `:338–344` defines `navigateHandler` (`options?.external || options?.newTab` → `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`, otherwise react-router `navigate(url)` from `useNavigate()` at `:131`); `:723` passes it as `onNavigate`, and `:727` registers `handlers: { api, flow, script: serverActionHandler, modal }`.
- `packages/react/src/context/ActionContext.tsx:113` builds `new ActionRunner(normalizedContext)` and `:117` calls `r.setNavigationHandler(onNavigate)` (the same call in `packages/react/src/hooks/useActionRunner.ts`).
- `packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts`: `execute` calls `handlePostExecution(action, result)` on every path — the update-operation path (`:1214`), the registered custom handler path (`:1222`, which is where the console's `api` and `script` handlers return), the built-in path (`:1246`) and the catch (`:1250`). `handlePostExecution` (`:1302`) at `:1411–1416` does `if (result.success && action.onSuccess) { const navigation = readOnSuccessNavigation(action.onSuccess); if (navigation) this.navigateOnSuccess(navigation, action, result); }`. `readOnSuccessNavigation` (`:2275`, exported) accepts only an object whose `navigate` is a non-empty string. `navigateOnSuccess` (`:1447–1483`) interpolates `block.navigate` through `interpolateTarget(block.navigate, action, readActionPayload(result.data))` (the `${result.*}` scope is passed by this one caller, beside `${param.*}` / `${ctx.*}`), refuses a URL that is not `http://`, `https://`, `/` or `./` (`isValidUrl`), sets `const newTab = block.openIn === 'newTab'` with no fallback of its own, and calls `this.navigationHandler(url, { external, newTab })`, falling back to `window.open` / `result.redirect` only when no handler is registered.
- Producer leg: `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx:270` forwards `onSuccess: schema.onSuccess` into the def it hands to `execute` (`:273`); `action-icon.tsx` carries the same `onSuccess: schema.onSuccess` (1 hit); `action-menu.tsx:284` and `action-group.tsx:286` forward `onSuccess: action.onSuccess` per rendered item. `packages/app-shell/src/views/DeclaredActionsBar.tsx:257` destructures `const { params: rawParams, ...rest } = action`, builds `dispatch = { ...localizeActionTexts(objectName, rest), objectName, params }` (`:286–296`; the localizer itself spreads `...action`, `packages/react/src/hooks/useActionTextLocalizer.ts:29`, so `onSuccess` rides through) and calls `execute(dispatch)` (`:322`); `DeclaredActionButton` is defined at `:114` and rendered at `:502`. `DeclaredActionsBar` is mounted by `RecordDetailView.tsx:2500` and `apps/console/src/pages/system/ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx:2488/2535`; `type: 'action:bar'` is rendered by `ObjectView.tsx:3106`, `InterfaceListPage.tsx:566` and `environment/EnvironmentListToolbar.tsx:125/264`.
- The `script` handler's file at the pin is `packages/app-shell/src/utils/consoleServerAction.ts`; at `:240` `if (readOnSuccessNavigation(action.onSuccess))` it defers to the declared block instead of also following a handler-returned `redirectUrl`, which is what the `navigate` row's note says. The spec refuses `onSuccess` together with `opensInNewTab: true` (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts:1960`).

`action.onSuccess.navigate` — the row's evidence (`ActionRunner.ts#handlePostExecution`, `#navigateOnSuccess`, `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx#useConsoleActionRuntime`) and producer (the four renderers plus `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx#DeclaredActionButton`) all resolve to the symbols and reads above. RIGHT.

`action.onSuccess.openIn` — evidence `ActionRunner.ts#navigateOnSuccess` (`block.openIn === 'newTab'`, 1 hit) and `useConsoleActionRuntime` (`options?.newTab` → new window, otherwise `navigate`); producer `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts#ActionSchema` (`openIn: z.enum(['self', 'newTab'], …).default('self')` at `:1649–1655`, materialized) plus the renderer forward. RIGHT.

`translation.flows.screens` — mount chain, closed by hand at the pin:
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx` imports `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_COPY_KEYS` and `resolveFlowScreenTitle` from the spec (`:138–139`). `activeFlowsBundle` (`:185`) reads `i18n.getResourceBundle(language, 'translation')`, walks its namespaces and returns `{ [language]: { flows } }` when `flows[flowName]` exists. `localizeScreen` (`:219`) computes the title through `resolveFlowScreenTitle(bundle, flowName, screen, { locale: language })` (`:226`) and `fieldCopy = bundle[language]?.flows?.[flowName]?.screens?.[screen.nodeId]?.fields` (`:227`), overlaying each field over `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_COPY_KEYS` (`label`, `placeholder`; spec `i18n-resolver.ts:3378`), each key falling back to the authored value. `FlowRunner` (`:294`) computes `shown = localizeScreen(screen, flowName, activeFlowsBundle(i18n, language, flowName), language)` (`:324`), draws `shown.title` as the `DialogTitle` (`:462`) and hands `screen={shown}` to `ScreenView` (`:495–496`).
- The `FlowRunner` element is mounted (non-test JSX, `git grep` at the pin) in exactly three places: `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:798` inside the `dialogs` element (`:734–818`) that `ConsoleShell` renders, and that `ObjectView.tsx:1506` and `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx:552` render through their own `useConsoleActionRuntime(…)` calls; `RecordDetailView.tsx:2628` (RecordDetailView is mounted by app-shell `console/AppContent.tsx:1096`, `ObjectView.tsx:3326`, `ObjectDataPage.tsx:626`, `InterfaceListPage.tsx:588`); and `apps/console/src/pages/developer/FlowRunsPage.tsx:410`, routed at `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx:169` (`developer/flow-runs`) and registered as `developer:flow-runs` (`registerDeveloperComponents.tsx:49–54`). The flow handler sets `screenFlow = { flowName, runId, screen }` when a run pauses at a screen node (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:612`).
- Bundle leg: `apps/console/src/loadLanguage.ts:16–19` fetches `/api/v1/i18n/translations/${lang}` and runs `transformSpecTranslations(translations)`; `packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-translations.ts` lists `'flows'` among the recognised spec groups (`:84`) and its generic forward loop (`:211–214`) copies every top-level key it did not flatten — `flows` is not in `PASSTHROUGH_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` (`:122–128`) and not `objects`, so it is copied verbatim — into `appNs`, returned as `{ app: appNs }`; `packages/i18n/src/provider.tsx:669–671` (`I18nProvider`, `:565`) adds the loaded payload with `addResourceBundle(currentLang, 'translation', resources, true, true)`, which is the tree `activeFlowsBundle` walks. Server leg in this repo at the head: `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts#loadTranslations` (`:1989`) hands each locale's data whole to `i18nService.loadTranslations(locale, data)` (`:2131`); `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts#handleI18nRequest` (`:35`) answers `getTranslations(locale)` whole (`:76`, `:85`). The local evidence `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts#resolveFlowScreenTitle` exists at `:3458`.

Per-read control (`git show REF:PATH | grep -cF`), pin / `256b4c9e` / `origin/main 972c1685`: `readOnSuccessNavigation(action.onSuccess)` 1/1/1, `private navigateOnSuccess(` 1/1/1, `block.navigate` 2/2/2, `block.openIn === 'newTab'` 1/1/1, `onSuccess: schema.onSuccess` (action-button) 1/1/1, `resolveFlowScreenTitle(bundle, flowName, screen` 1/1/1, `?.screens?.[screen.nodeId]?.fields` 1/1/1, `function activeFlowsBundle` 1/1/1, `FlowRunner` in useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx 4/4/4, `useConsoleActionRuntime({ dataSource })` in ConsoleShell.tsx 1/1/1, `ConsoleShell` in App.tsx 4/4/4, `'flows',` in spec-translations.ts 1/1/1, `transformSpecTranslations(translations)` 1/1/1, `setNavigationHandler(onNavigate)` in ActionContext.tsx and useActionRunner.ts 1/1/1 each. Every cited file exists at the pin. The history citations resolve: objectui#5493, #5934 and #5920 are closed issues with the titles the notes describe; objectui#5221 is cited by `ActionRunner.ts:1395` itself at the pin as "the console half of objectstack#9566/#9474", its events and timeline resolve (labelled `domain:ui`, closed 2026-08-24, landed by objectui PR #5933 "read ActionSchema.onSuccess for post-success navigation"), though the issue body itself answers 404 to this token; objectstack #9566, #9474, #7646 and #11287 are closed; #20318 is open (`domain:spec`, `priority:p3`, `area:i18n`).

**2. The `flows` container stays `planned` + `authorWarn`, its new `authorHint` is true, `translation.flows.label` stays `planned` — RIGHT.**

Structural walk of `translation.json` base → head: the `flows` container changed only `authorHint` and `note`; `status` `planned`, `authorWarn: true` and `verifiedAt` `2026-08-11` are unchanged. The `flows.label` row is byte-identical to base (`status: planned`, no `authorWarn`). The new hint carries no tracker number (regex `#\d+` over the string: none); #20318 is cited in the appended `note` sentence. Its two claims were checked at the pin: "the console's screen-flow runner reads `screens`: each screen's `title` and each field's `label` / `placeholder` render in the active locale" is the `localizeScreen` → `DialogTitle` / `ScreenView` path above; "the flow's own `label` is read by nothing yet" — a census over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` at the pin for any `flows…label` read finds none (the only `.flows` reads are FlowRunner `:194` / `:227` and two unrelated flow-list payloads in `packagedFlows.ts` and `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`), and in this repo the only reader of `flows.FLOW.label` is the unexported `lookupFlowLabel` (`i18n-resolver.ts:3382`), reachable only through `translateFlow` (`:3536`), which is not in the `translateMetadataDocument` dispatch table (view, action, object, app, dashboard, dataset, page, …; no flow) and has no caller outside its own test. Lint's `shouldWarn` (`packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.ts:157–159`) warns on `authorWarn === true || status === 'experimental'` only, and its hint is `entry.authorHint ?? entry.note ?? defaultHint` (`:390`), so the bit's readers see the new text and the same warn set: a walk of both ledgers for `authorWarn === true` gives `translation: ["flows"]`, `action: []` at base and at head alike.

**3. `check:liveness` at the head exits 0, `state-counts.md` is current, no row lost a reader or became `live` without one — RIGHT.**

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:liveness` at the head: exit 0; `action 49 classified (live 46, dead 3)`; `translation 24 classified (live 23, planned 1)`; `evidence paths: 617 repo-local … 617 resolved … 223 attributed to another repo`; `symbol anchors: 764 … 764`; `container coverage: 109 … 564`; `✓ packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md is current — the same 40 row(s)`. `gen:liveness-counts` rewrote `state-counts.md` byte-identically (`git diff` empty). Control 1, base `action.json` / `translation.json` / `state-counts.md` swapped in: exit 0, `translation 24 (live 22, planned 2)`, 616/616 local, 218 foreign, 760/760 anchors. Control 2, base ledgers with the head `state-counts.md`: exit 1, `state-counts.md is STALE`, so the freshness check is lit. `--producer-gap`: 96 live entries cite a producer (93 before this PR per the round-one report: the three flipped rows). CI `Spec property liveness` at the head (job 108723199441): success, with the same `action 49 classified (live 46, dead 3)`, `translation 24 classified (live 23, planned 1)`, 617/617, 764/764, 96 producer-citing and `state-counts.md is current` lines.

Structural walk base → head: `action.json` 42 leaf rows, `live 37 / dead 3 / planned 2` → `live 39 / dead 3`; exactly two rows changed, `onSuccess.navigate` and `onSuccess.openIn`, each `planned → live` with `evidence` and `producer` added, `verifiedAt` `2026-08-18 → 2026-09-27`, `evidenceScope` `cross-repo` kept, `authorWarn` absent before and after. `translation.json` 17 leaf rows, `live 15 / planned 2` → `live 16 / planned 1`; `flows.screens` `planned → live` with `evidence`, `producer`, `evidenceScope: cross-repo` added and `verifiedAt` `2026-08-11 → 2026-09-27`; the `flows` container changed text only. No row lost an `evidence` field, no `live` row became anything else, no `authorWarn` changed, no row was added or removed, `undrilled-containers.baseline.json` is untouched and the container coverage figure did not move.

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:objectui-pin-citations` at the head, with `../objectui` a symlink to the read-only clone: exit 0, `47 asserting objectui pin citation(s) match .objectui-sha (f8a9d0fb0), 53 historical citation(s) recorded and not checked, across 1653 spec source(s)`, `7 anchor content assertion(s) verified against objectui at f8a9d0fb0`. Control with the three base `src` files restored: `47 asserting / 50 historical`, and the diff adds exactly three sentences of the historical form (the "`.objectui-sha` pin `f8a9d0fb`" prose in the three JSDoc blocks), so the +3 is accounted for and no asserting citation was added or moved.

**4. The three `src` files change only in comments, and the new prose is true at the pin — RIGHT.**

`typescript` 6.0.3 `transpileModule` with `removeComments: true`, ES2022 / ESNext, over base and head: `ui/action.zod.ts` raw `b2e1bac74f25c62c → 507f9472d8594d49` (differ), stripped `458e751a64bf8ce4 = 458e751a64bf8ce4` (44830 bytes both); `system/translation.zod.ts` raw `9a0c42ff0deefd8b → fdf2c86eb835e160`, stripped `a9fe3aa64c3a71e2 = a9fe3aa64c3a71e2` (43247 bytes); `system/i18n-resolver.ts` raw `237136a3535d48ac → 0b3352a545656c2d`, stripped `5680cc3e05cebe9a = 5680cc3e05cebe9a` (55520 bytes). Controls the instrument sees, per file: an appended `export const` changes every stripped hash (`1df4dfb2…`, `bf6fbf3d…`, `2d7def94…`); a one-token code mutation changes it too (`translation.zod.ts` `b8c4425e…`, `i18n-resolver.ts` `e59daf5b…`, `action.zod.ts` `'self'` → `'selg'` on the code line at `:1655` gives `5b572270fa883170` — see the control note in ③).

Prose, checked at the pin: the `onSuccess` JSDoc names `ActionRunner` (`handlePostExecution` → `readOnSuccessNavigation` → `navigateOnSuccess`), the three interpolation scopes, the handoff to the console's router and a new tab only on `openIn: 'newTab'` — each is a line quoted in ①. The `flows` JSDoc says `FlowRunner` reads `screens` (`title`, `label`, `placeholder`), the flow's own `label` is read by nothing, `screens` is `live` and `label` `planned` — true per ② and the ledger at the head. The `translateFlow` docblock says the #11287 runner card took the client side (objectui#5920, "the runner half of objectstack#11287 (client-side pick)", closed), that `FlowRunner` overlays `flows.FLOW.screens` at the pin, that this function stays unregistered (not in the dispatch table, no callers) and that `flows.FLOW.label` has no reader on either side yet — true per ②. `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors` at the head: exit 0, 3768 anchors resolve, 3 cross-repo. `check:doc-authoring` exit 0.

**5. The lint and CLI flow-liveness pins do not move; `authorWarnedProperties('translation')` is still `["flows"]` — RIGHT.**

Static half: the warn set is derived from the shipped ledgers alone (`authorWarnedProperties` = keys of `loadWarnMap(dir, type)`, `lint-liveness-properties.ts:369–373`; `authorWarnedTranslationGroups()` = its top-level members, `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts:1082–1085`, consumed at `:1455` to hold back the `flows.*` demand), and the walk in ② gives the same `["flows"]` for `translation` and `[]` for `action` at base and head, so the assertions `authorWarnedProperties('translation').has('flows')` (`packages/lint/src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts:1316`) and `[...authorWarnedTranslationGroups()]` equals `['flows']` (`packages/cli/test/i18n-flow-liveness-gate.test.ts:123`) cannot change on this diff. Dynamic half, run at the head under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (VERDICT `command-exit 0`, held 60s, waited 285s on the second attempt; the first attempt exited 99 after its 540s budget), after `OS_SKIP_DTS=1 pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/lint --filter=@objectstack/platform-objects --filter=@objectstack/metadata-core --concurrency=2` (8 tasks successful: types, spec, core, formula, sdui-parser, metadata-core, lint, platform-objects): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/lint-liveness-properties.test.ts src/component-field-specs-liveness.test.ts` exit 0, `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 91 passed (91)`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2 test/i18n-flow-liveness-gate.test.ts test/i18n-flow-screen-coverage.test.ts` exit 0, `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 29 passed (29)`. Both counts equal the dev's, so no pin moved. Built-lint probe from the lint source over the built spec: `authorWarnedProperties('translation')` is `["flows"]` and `authorWarnedProperties('action')` is `[]`; a stack whose `zh-CN` bundle authors `flows.lead_conversion.screens.s1.title` and a field `label` draws exactly one finding, rule `liveness-planned-property`, message unchanged ("sets `flows` but this translation property is planned — declared, and a consumer is being built against it (not read YET)."), `hint` byte-equal to the head `translation.json` `flows.authorHint`; the same stack against a copy of the ledger directory with the base `action.json` / `translation.json` swapped in draws the same one finding with the old hint ("No shipped screen-flow runner reads this group yet …"). An `api` action authoring `onSuccess: { navigate, openIn: 'newTab' }` draws 0 findings against either ledger set.
